title: console app header: a view stored with no label is titled by its humanized qualified name ("Recheck Gate.Default") on the /view/NAME route, while its tab now reads the object plural label (objectui#12774)
body:
Filing gate ①: a class-a finding from the os-dev report on objectui#12774 (PR #12804, `out_of_scope_findings[0]`). Filed by the `domain:ui` seat 1 (`session_011K9g23W67dy2zwnyzaoB6o`). ⛔ Not a claim; for triage to grade and route.

reach: static read only (NOT MEASURED in a browser: the published `18.0.0-next.2` backend still invents a view `label` from its `name`, so no label-less view is served there yet). It is the sibling of objectui#12774, whose PR names a label-less view by the object's plural label on the tab, the mobile switcher and the record page's way back.

## Static read (objectui `main` `a8add5c`)

- `packages/app-shell/src/layout/AppHeader.tsx:717`: on a `/apps/APP/OBJECT/view/NAME` route, the header's title falls back to `(viewDef && (viewDef.label || viewDef.title)) || humanizeSlug(viewName)`.
- `humanizeSlug` (`:111`) turns `recheck_gate.default` into "Recheck Gate.Default": a string derived from the machine name.
- Once objectstack PR #24013 (`aefab7c2c6`) is in the runtime the console talks to, a view stored with no `label` is served with no `label` key, so the header and the tab name the same view two different ways.

## For triage to scope

- objectui#12774's rule (the object's plural label for every label-less view, never the qualified name) is the likely target, so the header and the tab agree. The header already resolves `currentObject`; whether it can reach the same plural label without a second derivation is the claimant's to measure.
- The same function falls back to `humanizeSlug` for dashboards (`:662`), pages (`:674`) and reports (`:683`). Whether those surfaces have the same label-less case is not measured here.

Dedupe: `search_issues` in objectui with "app header view title humanizeSlug label-less view route title qualified name" returned 4: objectui#12774 (the tab, its sibling) and three closed cards on other surfaces (#11196, #8813, #2217). None covers the header title.
